subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool routing surface now, or keep cross-gateway session messaging behind the broader federation/security design work?
rationale: The PR adds new model-visible tool parameters, a config map, and cross-gateway session control, which changes the Gateway trust boundary and cannot be safely accepted by patch review alone.

options.title: Pause for federation design
options.body: Keep this PR open or close it after maintainer review while using the linked issue and federation FRD to define peer identity, scopes, URL policy, and session-state semantics first.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow replacement
options.body: A maintainer can bless a smaller peer-routing contract and ask for a refreshed PR that fixes the protocol defects, keeps the URL/auth boundary explicit, and includes live two-gateway proof.

options.title: Accept the narrow surface
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally own `gateway.peers` as an operator-only feature, but should still require the correctness fixes and real behavior proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Pause for federation design
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open or close it after maintainer review while using the linked issue and federation FRD to define peer identity, scopes, URL policy, and session-state semantics first.

likelyOwner.reason: The session-tool/gateway override history most consistently points to this owner for the product and security boundary decision.
